\section{Interaction sample 1: Gradient updates}

Each section is a self-contained synthetic example for testing the
editor. Read the paragraph, move the pointer across several lines,
and select a phrase in either direction. Every sentence was written
for this demonstration; no personal manuscript, unpublished result,
or private file is included.

The model uses a vector of real variables and a smooth quadratic objective.
The displayed expressions are native editable formula insets. Clicking
inside a formula should place the mathematical cursor at the requested
symbol. Scrolling past the equation should preserve its spacing, subscripts,
and surrounding text.

\[
f_{1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_{i}-b_{i})^{2},\qquad\nabla f_{1}(x)=x-b.
\]

To test sustained scrolling, move through several sections without
pausing, then reverse direction. Observe whether the content continues
moving after the wheel has stopped. A delayed response can indicate
queued input, while an increasingly irregular display may indicate
work in frame capture, transport, or presentation.

To test a growing selection, begin near the top of the document and
drag toward the lower edge of the viewport. Keep the button held as
the editor scrolls into later sections. The highlighted range should
follow the pointer, and releasing the button should end the gesture
promptly.

\[
x_{k+1}=x_{k}-\alpha_{k}\nabla f_{1}(x_{k}),\qquad r_{k}=\left\Vert x_{k+1}-x_{k}\right\Vert _{2}.
\]

Open the Review panel and repeat the same gesture. Reading annotations
should not interrupt the active selection. After releasing the pointer,
the review list and prepared clipboard may catch up. An explicit request
to create a comment must still capture the complete selected passage
at that moment.

This document intentionally mixes prose, headings, short lists, and
mathematics. Its PDF uses explicit page breaks to provide exactly
twenty-five numbered pages. The continuous LyX editing view does not
display PDF page boundaries, so compare the numbered section headings
when repeating an interaction or reporting a delayed response.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Checkpoint 1. Select one sentence, then reverse the selection direction.
\item Release the pointer, pause, and verify that scrolling and highlighting
stop.
\end{enumerate}
